name: Ultra-low-cost freeze-dried enzymes for synthetic biology

mentions.name: Ultra-low-cost freeze-dried enzymes for synthetic biology
mentions.description: This project produces ultra-low-cost freeze-dried enzymes for synthetic biology. Roughly $30 of culture media can yield more than 10,000,000 reactions worth of PCR enzyme using a purpose-built strain and equipment; QC (normally very expensive by hand) is being automated and enzymes are lyophilized for super simple logistics. The intended workflow is a daily-use tube placed on a lab robot that handles that day's PCR reactions and is thrown out the next day, cutting the per-reaction price from $1 to $0.01 while greatly simplifying logistics.
mentions.problem: PCR reactions cost about $1 each, which seems negligible at small lab scale but becomes a major expense when scaling up with robots; hand-done QC is very expensive and logistics are complicated.
mentions.audience: Labs scaling up PCR with robots
mentions.source_excerpt: I am working on making ultra-low cost freeze-dried enzymes for synthetic biology.
